features.name: File-system directory browsing
steps: Enter a common system folder such as Download from the root of internal storage
View the files and subfolders inside
Then enter second- and third-level directories
The top title or path state changes with the current directory
Use the back key to step back level by level
After returning to the parent directory the original files and directories are still correct. An empty directory should show an empty state rather than an error.
features.expected: The title or path changes with the current directory; the back key steps back level by level to the correct parent directory; an empty directory shows an empty state; the list content matches the actual file system.

features.name: Storage location and document-source switching
steps: Open the left navigation drawer
Switch between entries such as "recent, images, videos, audio, documents, downloads, and internal storage"
After selecting internal storage the real root directory is shown
When selecting a document source provided by another app, the browsing content switches to the corresponding provider
Returning to internal storage restores the local file tree. Different sources must not be wrongly merged into the same physical directory.
features.expected: After switching entries the real content of the corresponding source is shown; internal storage shows the real root directory; content from different document sources must not be merged; returning to internal storage restores the local file tree.

features.name: Create a new folder
steps: Tap "new folder" in the menu in a writable directory
Enter a legal directory name
Confirm
The new folder appears in the current directory immediately
Enter that folder to confirm it is empty
It still exists after returning to the parent directory
It still exists after fully exiting and reopening the file manager. For duplicate directory names, illegal names, etc. reasonable feedback should be given rather than creating an abnormal directory.
features.expected: The new folder must genuinely be written to the file system and still exist after exiting and re-entering; duplicate or illegal names give reasonable feedback; a failure must not leave an abnormal directory.

features.name: Renaming files and folders
steps: Select an ordinary file or a self-created folder
Select "rename"
Enter a new name
After confirming, the name in the list updates
The file content and directory content must not be lost
After re-entering the directory the new name still exists. If only the extension was changed the file should keep its original byte content; after renaming a directory its subtree is still intact.
features.expected: After renaming the name genuinely updates without losing the file content; when only the extension is changed the byte content stays the same; after renaming a directory its subtree is intact; a duplicate name should give feedback.

features.name: File copy
steps: Prepare a source file
Select and use "copy to…" or copy
Select another target directory, e.g. copy from Download to Documents
After the operation completes the source file still exists
A copy with identical content appears in the target directory
The two files can be modified independently afterwards. Copying a folder should recursively copy its internal hierarchy and files.
features.expected: The source file is preserved and a copy with identical content appears in the target directory; the two files can be modified independently; copying a folder recursively copies its internal hierarchy.

features.name: File move
steps: Select a file or folder
Use "move to…" or cut
Select the target directory
After the move completes the object disappears from the source directory
The object appears in the target directory
The file content stays consistent
When a folder is moved all its subdirectories and files move with it
The old copy is no longer visible at the original location.
features.expected: After moving, the source location disappears, the target location appears with identical content; the folder's internal contents move as a whole; the old copy is not visible at the original location.

features.name: Cut / copy / paste loop
steps: Select an object
Perform copy or cut
Navigate to another directory
The "paste" state becomes available
Paste
In copy mode the source and target both exist while in cut mode the source disappears
Repeated pasting, cancelling, and switching directories preserve or invalidate the clipboard state reasonably.
features.expected: Paste is only available when the clipboard has content; in copy mode the source and target both exist while in cut mode the source disappears; repeated pasting matches the mode; the clipboard state is reasonably preserved or invalidated when switching directories.

features.name: Delete files and directories
steps: Create files and subfolders for testing
Single or multiple selection
Delete
A confirmation flow appears
After confirming, the object disappears from the real directory
It still does not exist after refreshing and re-entering the directory. Deleting a non-empty directory should handle its contents too; clicking cancel must not actually delete anything.
features.expected: After confirming, the object disappears from the real directory and does not reappear after refreshing; deleting a non-empty directory handles its contents too; clicking cancel must not delete anything.

features.name: Multi-select and batch file operations
steps: Long-press a file to enter selection mode
Then tap several files/folders
The selection count changes in real time
Use "select all" to select all selectable items in the current directory
Perform copy, move, delete, or share on the multi-selected results
The operation applies to all selected objects
Exit the selection state after completing or cancelling.
features.expected: The selection count is accurate in real time; select-all includes all selectable items in the current directory; batch operations apply to all selected objects; the selection state exits after completing or cancelling.

features.name: File search
steps: Create files and directories with distinguishable names in internal storage
Tap search
Enter the full name or a name fragment
The results converge in real time
The search results can include matching files and directories
Tapping a result opens the corresponding object
Clearing the search restores normal browsing. The search must not merely filter the current screen's text but should at least cover the genuinely accessible documents within the current search scope.
features.expected: The results cover genuinely accessible documents rather than only the current screen's text; entering a name fragment converges the results; tapping a result opens the corresponding object; clearing the search restores normal browsing.

features.name: Type and quick filtering
steps: Prepare images, videos, audio, ordinary documents, and other file types in storage
Tap the "images, audio, video, documents" filter chips at the top in turn
The current results keep only the corresponding MIME/media type
When "large files" is toggled, filter by the file-size condition
When "this week" is toggled, filter by the time condition
All content is restored after clearing the filters.
features.expected: Each filter keeps only the corresponding MIME or media type; large files and this week take effect by size and time conditions; clearing the filters restores all content; filtering does not modify files.

features.name: Sort rules
steps: Prepare several items with different names, sizes, modification times, and types in the same directory
Open "sort mode"
Test file name A in turn
Z / Z
A, newer modification date
Old / old
New, type A
Z / Z
A, larger size
Small / small
Large
After each sort an order change consistent with the rule can be observed
The directory's own content is not modified.
features.expected: Each sort mode genuinely changes the order and matches the rule, with forward and reverse giving opposite results; sorting does not modify the directory content; the sort state stays consistent after switching directories.

features.name: Grid and list display
steps: In a directory containing folders, ordinary files, and images
Tap the view-switch button on the right
Switch the grid layout to the list layout
Then switch back to grid
The file and directory sets stay exactly consistent
Images show a thumbnail when thumbnails are supported, and ordinary files show a type icon
Switching modes must not change the sort, current directory, or actual files.
features.expected: Grid and list show the same file set and switching does not change the sort or current directory; images show thumbnails and ordinary files show type icons; the file set is exactly the same after switching.

features.name: Hidden-file display
steps: Prepare ordinary and hidden files in an accessible directory
The default state is displayed according to the app's current rules
Select "show hidden files" in the menu
Hidden objects appear
Then select "don't show hidden files" and it disappears
Toggling the hidden state may only change the display result and must not delete, move, or rename hidden files.
features.expected: After toggling, hidden objects appear or disappear; only the display changes and hidden files are not deleted, moved, or renamed; after re-entering the directory the state matches the setting.

features.name: Viewing file/folder information
steps: Select a folder
"Get info"
The info page shows the name, type, modification time, item count, etc.
For an ordinary file show the corresponding file type, size, and other metadata

The information matches the actual object. For objects exposed by a provider, it should also correctly reflect whether create, delete, move, rename, metadata, etc. are supported according to its capabilities, rather than hard-coding the same set of values for all.
features.expected: The info page data matches the actual object; folders show the item count while files show the type and size; the capability flags of different document sources must be truly reflected rather than all hard-coded.

features.name: File opening and "open with"
steps: Select a file with a clear type
Tap open
The system lists the apps able to handle the file by MIME type
Select the target app
The content is passed to the target app and can be read
After returning to the file manager it is still in a reasonable directory state. The candidate app sets should differ for different file types.
features.expected: List the apps able to handle the file by MIME type, with different candidate sets per type; the content is correctly passed to the target app; after returning it remains in a reasonable directory state.

features.name: Recent-file aggregation
steps: First visit several files in different directories
Open "recent"
Recently accessed/generated files appear in an aggregated view without requiring the user to know their original folder
Files can be opened directly from the recent page
The file still corresponds to the original storage object rather than producing an extra copy
After the original file is deleted, "recent" must not permanently keep a fake entry that still opens normally.
features.expected: The recent list corresponds to the original storage object rather than a copy; files can be opened directly from recent; after the original file is deleted, recent must not keep a fake entry that still opens normally.

features.name: System file pick/save loop
steps: Trigger "open file" or "save as" from another app
DocumentsUI launches in the system picker mode
Can navigate between "recent, downloads, internal storage, and other document sources"
In open mode, select an existing file and return the correct URI to the caller; in save mode, enter the file name, choose a directory, and save

Return to the file manager to verify the new file genuinely exists. If the caller requested directory selection, only a legal directory may be confirmed and an ordinary file must not be returned as a directory.
features.expected: Open mode returns the correct file URI to the caller; save mode genuinely writes the new file into the chosen directory; directory selection may only return a legal directory; on cancel the caller receives an explicit result.
